title: Noetherianity and maximal-local regularity of a henselization of a G-ring
statement: Let A be a G-ring and let c present the henselization of (A,I) as the filtered colimit of etale A-algebras trivial modulo I, with its henselian-pair and quotient-isomorphism properties. Then c.pt.right is Noetherian and every maximal ideal m of c.pt.right has a regular map from the localization at m to its adic completion.

proof.text: Install base Noetherianity from the G-ring hypothesis. Apply pair_henselization_noetherian_completion to the given colimit, obtaining Noetherianity of B and flatness of its structure map f.

For a maximal ideal m of B, the henselian-pair hypothesis places J=IB in m. Quotient surjectivity supplies, for every b in B, an a in A with b-f(a) in J. With p=f inverse(m), subtraction and ideal-map monotonicity prove pB=m. Localize f to phi:A_p to B_m. It is flat by the localization theorem for flat maps. The equality pB=m identifies extended maximal ideals. Represent an element of the residue field of B_m by b in B, then by the above a, proving residue-field surjectivity; injectivity is the local-map quotient injectivity theorem. Apply flat_local_completion_iso to obtain the commuting completion equivalence e.

The completion map A_p to its completion is regular by the G-ring hypothesis. Compose with the regular localization A to A_p; the completion is Noetherian and all composite fibres are Noetherian. Transport this regular map along e using regular-ring-map equivalence transport. The commuting completion square identifies the result with g composed with f, where g is B to B_m to completion(B_m).

Apply pair_henselization_regular_fibers to g and the regular composite. Compose flatness of B to B_m and of the Noetherian local completion map to obtain flatness of g. These two assertions give regularity of g by the definition. Cancel B to B_m using regular-through-localization, obtaining regularity of the required maximal local completion map. Combine with Noetherianity from step 1.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0AH3: quotient representatives establish the omitted local completion comparison; the final tensor calculation is isolated in the regular-fibres node. Lean combines comparison, regular composition, equivalence transport and localization cancellation.
